info.title: Acta API
info.description: Acta's operator API, the one the dashboard uses. Lists page by cursor: pass a page's nextCursor back as cursor until hasMore is false; a cursor is tied to its query. Every POST, PUT, and DELETE is a control, mapped only where the host enables controls, and where the host requires it the call carries the confirmation header the operation lists, with the value true. A control whose request object is optional acts with its defaults when the request has no body; one that declares application/json and sends no bytes answers 400, so send {} or leave the content type off. A signal raise takes any JSON value instead, and no bytes, with or without the content type, raise a presence-only signal. POST /jobs answers 201 when it inserted the job and 200 when a deduplication key matched an existing one, with the job's URL in Location either way. A string carrying x-acta-known-values is an open set: compare against the known values and keep any other value as it is. The document declares no security scheme: the host adds its own authentication, which a client sends as the host asks.

AcknowledgeAlertResponse.description: What acknowledging an alert did, and its timestamps after the attempt.

ActaControlConfirmation.description: The one value a control's confirmation header carries.

AlertDeliveryStatusCode.description:
Delivery state of one alert row. Numeric bands are a readability convention only; behavior
follows the explicit members.

Known values:
- unspecified: Alert delivery status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- pending: Materialized; awaiting the first send attempt.
- retry-after: Send deferred until the alert's retry_after_utc instant.
- suppressed: Intentionally not sent because process-local channel policy rejected delivery.
- delivered: Successfully sent to the channel transport.
- failed: Send attempt failed and the retry path is done with it; re-sent as a reminder while the incident stays unresolved.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

AlertKindCode.description:
What condition an alert reports. Sparse catalog ids leave insertion room; numeric ordering is
not behavioral.

Known values:
- unspecified: Alert kind not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- first-failure: Failure that opened the incident; emitted by Automatic origin on non-terminal failure.
- threshold-reached: Threshold-bound emission (e.g., LostClaimAlertThreshold reached).
- final-failure: Terminal failure; emitted by Automatic origin on Status to Failed.
- manual: Hand-raised; ctx.AlertAsync from inside a handler.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

AlertOriginCode.description:
Known values:
- unspecified: Alert origin not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- automatic: System-emitted from a state-mutating SP (failure / timeout / orphan / deadline).
- manual: ctx.AlertAsync from inside a user handler.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

AlertProfileCode.description:
Known values:
- none: No automatic failure alerts. ctx.AlertAsync still creates rows.
- on-failure: Default. Alerts on every failed or orphaned attempt; repeats collapse onto the job's one open incident. Final exhaustion writes a separate alert (a different reason yields a different DeduplicationKey). Every enabled profile records the attempts its alerts read whatever the event recording level, so an alert never depends on recording. Resolves on recovery, the job's next success.
- info: Informational alerts on terminal failure only; low severity. A recurring slot rarely reaches one - see on-terminal. Resolves on recovery, the job's next success.
- on-terminal: Alert on terminal failure only: retry budget exhausted, ctx.FailAsync, a non-retryable exception, or an interrupted at-most-once step, or a lost lease that spent the budget. Resolves on recovery, the job's next success. A deadline lands the job Cancelled rather than Failed and so alerts under no profile. A recurring slot never exhausts a budget and re-arms after an unhandled exception or a lost lease, so use on-failure to hear about those.
- sys-critical: Reserved for system Jobs. Emits at Severity = Critical to the Job's channel, or the configured "default" channel when none is declared.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

AlertRef.description:
Public stable reference for one alert row: "alr_" plus the Guid's 32 lowercase hex digits, such as
`alr_01a14f5038c17d0e9b2f6a4c81d3e5f7`. Dashboards, HTTP APIs, and alert transports address
alerts by this value; the numeric alert id stays the internal engine identity. Deduplication never
re-mints it: a condition that re-fires while its incident is open keeps that incident's ref.

AlertSeverityCode.description:
Known values:
- unspecified: Alert severity not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- info: Informational; not paging.
- warning: Non-terminal failure transition; repeats collapse onto the one open incident.
- error: Terminal failure or operator-attention event.
- critical: Highest severity; emitted by system Jobs (AlertProfile = SysCritical) and operator alerts for incidents. Whether it pages depends on the routed channel's transport and config.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

CalendarRoleCode.description:
What a catalog calendar family gives a schedule: its occurrences, or the windows they may fire in. The family's first
version fixes its role, and every newer version keeps it.

Known values:
- unspecified: Calendar role not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- occurrence: A calendar whose instants are a schedule's occurrences.
- availability: A calendar whose windows bound when a schedule's occurrences may fire.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

CalendarStatusCode.description:
Where one version of a catalog calendar family stands. At most one version of a family is Published at a time, and
that version is the family's current one; a version's content never changes, only its status.

Known values:
- unspecified: Calendar status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- draft: A saved version that was never published; no schedule follows it.
- published: The family's current version, the one its catalog-bound schedules follow.
- superseded: A version that was current until a newer one was published; history still pins it.
- archived: The family's current version, retired; the family has no current version until another is published.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

CalendarWindow.description:
One open range of an availability calendar: `[StartUtc, EndUtc)`, both UTC, the end after the start; a null
end is open forever.

CancelJobResponse.description: What cancelling a job did, and the job's status and version after the attempt.

CheckpointKindCode.description:
Discriminator for `checkpoints` rows: which durable substrate feature owns the
`(job_id, checkpoint_kind_code, checkpoint_name)` row. One physical table carries every simple job-internal
durable value; the kind keeps the name spaces structurally separate (a user variable can never
collide with a signal or a child latch of the same name).

Known values:
- unspecified: Checkpoint kind not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- variable: User variable; UPSERT, last-writer-wins, no state machine.
- signal: Signal; Pending while awaited, Set once raised.
- timer: Durable sleep timer; Pending until due, Consumed on replay past the due instant.
- progress: Progress; UPSERT, last-writer-wins, one per job.
- child-latch: Child terminal-outcome latch on the parent; Pending while awaited, Set when the child lands terminal.
- firing: The scheduler's firing envelope for a slot or scheduled root; Pending while outstanding, settled with the outcome; survives a handler reset.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

CheckpointStatusCode.description:
Known values:
- unspecified: Checkpoint status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- pending: Awaited or armed; the checkpoint has not been satisfied yet.
- set: Raised; the payload is stored and a waiting job proceeds.
- expired: The re-entering wait found the checkpoint overdue and settled it TimedOut; a raise then skips it.
- consumed: Due instant reached; the replayed handler consumed the timer and proceeded.
- succeeded: The firing settled successfully; the envelope is the slot's last outcome until the next admission replaces it.
- failed: The firing settled as a final failure; the envelope is the slot's last outcome until the next admission replaces it.
- cancelled: The firing settled by cancellation; the envelope is the slot's last outcome until the next admission replaces it.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

ControlAction.description:
Coarse outcome of a control verb: on jobs, schedules, definitions, alerts, the outbox, tags, tenants, and namespaces.

Known values: applied, not-found, rejected, accepted, version-conflict, already-in-state.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

DbProvider.description:
Known values: mssql, pg, sqlite.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

DeadlineBehaviorCode.description:
How the engine treats a job that has passed its deadline.

Known values:
- unspecified: Deadline behavior not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- strict: Engine auto-terminates an overdue job at admission and refuses to re-arm a retry past the deadline.
- advisory: Deadline is informational; the engine never auto-terminates, the handler reads ctx.IsOverdue.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

DefinitionPolicyOverrides.description:
The whole operator-override set for a definition's policy, applied as a unit: a non-null field sets its override
and null clears it back to the code default, so the dashboard reads, edits, and writes the full set. Code defaults,
contract, formats, and `definition_hash` are never touched. A `DeadlineSeconds` override on a scheduled
definition lands but is ignored: a deadline anchors to job creation, and a recurring slot lives forever.
`RateLimit` applies to every definition sharing the meter (declared `RateName`, or the name) in one
write, clearing included, so the meter never carries two rates.

DefinitionStatusCode.description:
Lifecycle status of a job definition. Numeric bands are a readability convention only;
behavior follows the explicit members. There is no per-definition Deprecated state by design:
operators pause individual Jobs via `IJobs.PauseAsync`.

Known values:
- unspecified: Definition status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- active: Enqueue allowed; claim allowed.
- retired: Enqueue REJECTED; an operator decision, never written by registration (a definition absent from a manifest stays Active). Retiring cancels parked rows (Ready/Paused/Suspended) with the event reason 'definition-retired'; in-flight executions finish their attempt, and a job that would run again lands Cancelled with the same reason.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

DiscardOutboxResponse.description: What parking a discard of a source's quarantined rows did.

EnqueueJobAction.description:
Coarse outcome classifier for one enqueued row.

Known values: inserted, deduplicated.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

input.description: Any JSON value, kept as sent.

EnqueueJobResponse.description:
What one enqueue answers: the internal long EnqueueJobResponse.JobId, the public JobRef EnqueueJobResponse.JobRef, and the
EnqueueJobAction EnqueueJobResponse.Action that tells a fresh insert from a match on string? EnqueueJobRequest.DeduplicationKey. A
batch answers one per request, in request order, in IReadOnlyList<EnqueueJobResponse> EnqueueJobsResponse.Jobs. A typed enqueue answers
the derived JobHandle.

EnqueueRejectionReason.description:
Why an enqueue was refused.

Known values: namespace-suspended, tenant-suspended, tenant-unknown, route-unknown, definition-retired, tenant-required, tenant-forbidden, tenant-mismatch, ancestor-lane, lane-isolation.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

EntityCode.description:
Names a kind of Acta entity, so one `(entity_code, entity_id)` pair can point at a row of any table. Tags
attach only to tenants, namespaces, definitions, and jobs, the targets TagTarget can build.

Known values:
- unspecified: Entity kind not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- alert: One alert.
- calendar: One version of a catalog calendar.
- checkpoint: One checkpoint of a job.
- definition: One job definition.
- event: One event.
- job: One job.
- lane: One lane.
- lock: One lock.
- namespace: One namespace.
- schedule: One schedule of a recurring job.
- step: One step of a job.
- tag: One tag on its entity.
- tenant: One tenant.
- worker: One worker process lifetime.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

EvaluationStatusCode.description:
Why a schedule's next evaluation is when it is: the scheduling engine's state for one schedule, distinct from the
operator lifecycle (ScheduleStatusCode) and from the slot job's status.

Known values:
- unspecified: Evaluation status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- scheduled: The next evaluation is the next nominal occurrence, or the end of a timed pause.
- waiting-for-capacity: An occurrence is due but the permanent slot is busy or the schedule is at its outstanding limit; settlement wakes it.
- exhausted: The source offers no further occurrence; a declaration or calendar change reactivates it.
- evaluation-error: The source could not be evaluated; the cursor is kept and the evaluation retries after a bounded delay.
- slot-unavailable: An occurrence is due but the permanent slot is held, cancelled, or failed terminally; a job resume or restart wakes it.
- resumed: An operator resumed the schedule; its first evaluation decides the backlog under the misfire policy and expires the stale part without pausing again.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

EventCode.description:
Stable family-local event identifiers. Nearby values improve catalog readability but carry no runtime subject,
subgroup, or outcome semantics; match events by enum member or textual code. There is no `job.enqueued`
event on purpose: the Job row's own `(created_at_utc, namespace_id, definition_id)` records the enqueue fact,
and a separate event row would be write amplification on the narrow append-heavy events table; dedup outcomes
reach the caller via `EnqueueJobResponse.Action`, and cross-job rate analytics query `acta.jobs` directly.

Known values:
- unspecified: Event id not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- tenant.suspended: An operator suspended a tenant; the name stops resolving at enqueue. EventMessage carries the reason.
- tenant.resumed: An operator resumed a suspended tenant; its key resolves at enqueue again. EventMessage carries the reason.
- tenant.updated: An operator changed a tenant display name / description. EventMessage carries the reason.
- namespace.suspended: An operator suspended a namespace; enqueue into it is rejected. EventMessage carries the reason.
- namespace.resumed: An operator resumed a suspended namespace; enqueue into it is allowed again. EventMessage carries the reason.
- namespace.updated: An operator changed a namespace owner team / description. EventMessage carries the reason.
- definition.overrides-updated: An operator changed a job definition's policy overrides; EventMessage summarizes the change.
- definition.retired: An operator retired a job definition; enqueue is rejected and its parked jobs were cancelled.
- job.execution-succeeded: The attempt's handler returned successfully; DurationMs is set. Audit records every one, Failures a success after counted failures, and an enabled alert profile also a one-shot's success past its first attempt.
- job.execution-failed: The attempt failed and the job lives on: a retry within budget, or a recurring job's firing that spent its budget and returned the slot to Idle. DurationMs and the failure's EventMessage are set; details carry reason and to.
- job.execution-orphaned: The attempt's worker lease expired and crash recovery reclaimed the job without ending it. WorkerId names the stale holder; details carry reason and to.
- job.execution-yielded: The attempt ended without succeeding or failing: rescheduled, suspended, paused, or cancelled by its handler or the engine. Audit only; details carry outcome and reason.
- job.failed: The job failed for good: its retry budget is spent, its handler failed it, or its failure is not retryable. DurationMs is set when an attempt ran; details carry reason.
- job.suspended: The attempt parked on a durable wait: a ctx.SleepAsync timer re-armed the job Ready at its due instant, or a signal or child wait left it Suspended. Budget-neutral; details carry to.
- job.rescheduled: The job re-armed Ready with a new NextRunAtUtc: a handler reschedule, a failed attempt's retry within budget, or an operator RescheduleAsync; details carry actor or reason.
- job.cancelled: Job was cancelled (Status to Cancelled, terminal).
- job.paused: Job was paused (Status to Paused).
- job.resumed: Job was resumed (Status to Ready).
- job.restarted: Job was restarted (Status to Ready; failure_count reset, retention cleared, execution_number unchanged).
- job.reprioritized: Operator changed the job's claim priority; EventMessage carries the operator's reason, if any.
- job.purged: Operator hard-deleted a terminal job; the subject is the deleted job's id. Details snapshot its jobRef, correlationKey, and actor. Always emitted regardless of event recording.
- job.input-amended: Operator amended a job's stored input payload; details carry the actor and bounded metadata (format name and byte count) about the previous payload, and EventMessage carries the why.
- job.signal-raised: Signal delivered via IJobs.RaiseSignalAsync; matching signal checkpoint (State = Set) UPSERTed.
- job.state-reset: Handler called ctx.ResetStateAsync; the job's checkpoints and steps were cleared so the next execution starts as new. The scheduler's firing envelope stays.
- job.note-recorded: Application-authored note from ctx.NoteAsync. The only event code an application can write and one the runtime never emits, so every other event stays provably system-written. EventMessage carries the line; details carry the optional payload.
- schedule.paused: A recurring schedule was paused; details carry the schedule name.
- schedule.resumed: A recurring schedule was resumed; details carry the schedule name.
- schedule.pause-expired: A timed pause elapsed; the scheduler auto-resumed the schedule. Details carry the schedule name.
- schedule.triggered: Operator admitted a manual firing of the slot; no schedule cursor moved. Details carry the schedule name.
- schedule.admitted: The admission engine selected one of the schedule's occurrences for a firing; details carry the schedule, the occurrence, the covered-through boundary, and the firing id.
- schedule.skipped: A range of the schedule's occurrences was decided without work: the misfire policy skipped it, it expired, the schedule was full, its calendar no longer produces it, or a calendar publication discarded it; details carry the schedule, the range, and the reason.
- schedule.retimed: A deploy changed the schedule's timing, or a calendar it names was published; the undecided occurrences of the old timing were discarded and the cursor moved to the first occurrence of the new one. Details carry the schedule name.
- calendar.draft-saved: An operator saved a new draft version of a catalog calendar. Details carry the calendar, the version, and the role; EventMessage carries the reason.
- calendar.published: An operator published a catalog calendar version, which became the family's current one. Details carry the calendar, the version, the version it replaced, the overdue decision, and the schedules it affected.
- calendar.archived: An operator archived a catalog calendar's current version; the family has no current version until another is published. Details carry the calendar and the version.
- worker.started: Worker process registered; a workers row was appended (Status: Active).
- worker.stopped: Worker process shut down cleanly (Status: Active/Draining to Stopped).
- worker.died: Worker heartbeat went stale; crash recovery flipped the worker to Dead.
- alert.acknowledged: Operator acknowledged an alert; EventMessage carries the note.
- alert.resolved: Operator manually resolved an alert; EventMessage carries the note.
- outbox.requeued: An operator command returned quarantined outbox rows to Pending; EventMessage carries the justification and the row ids.
- outbox.discarded: An operator command deleted quarantined outbox rows; EventMessage carries the justification and the deleted row ids.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

EventRecordingCode.description:
Known values:
- off: No recording-filtered per-job events; always-on system/catalog events still emit, and an enabled alert profile still records the failed, orphaned, terminally failed, and recovering attempts its alerts read.
- failures: Emit failed, orphaned, and terminally failed attempts, a success only when it recovers from counted failures, and lane repairs; suppress other recording-filtered per-job events.
- audit: Emit all recording-filtered per-job events. User Jobs default.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

ExplainJobAction.description:
A suggested operator move. string ExplainJobAction.Kind is a stable slug
(`raise-signal` | `cancel` | `resume` | `restart` | `inspect-timeline` |
`wait-recovery` | `none`); string ExplainJobAction.Description is the prose shown to the operator.

ExplainJobLease.description:
The execution lease on an Executing Job and the liveness of the worker holding it. When
bool ExplainJobLease.Expired is true the lease has lapsed and crash recovery reclaims the Job on its next pass;
string ExplainJobLease.RecoveryExpectation says so in prose. string? ExplainJobLease.WorkerName is the worker's deployment version, and
bool ExplainJobLease.WorkerStale is true once it has missed heartbeats past `JobsOptions.WorkerDeadAfter`. Both
WorkerRef? ExplainJobLease.WorkerRef and string? ExplainJobLease.WorkerName go null when retention purged the owner's row: the timings
still describe the Job, but the holder is unidentifiable.

ExplainJobResponse.description:
Plain-English explanation of a Job's current durable state: where the work is, why it moved there, and what an
operator can do next, assembled from the same `jobs_state`, `workers`, `steps`, `checkpoints`, and
`events` rows a `SELECT` would read. Returned by ValueTask<ExplainJobResponse?> IJobs.ExplainAsync(JobLookup job, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)); the CLI renders it as
prose, the dashboard as a panel. `StatusMeaning` is the `[Code]` description of `Status`; `ActiveWait`
and `Lease` are set only in their states, `LastExecutedBy` names the last worker when no lease is live, and
`Steps` are the newest int ExplainJobHandler.StepLimit, `StepsHasMore` saying older ones exist.

ExplainJobStep.description: One step's state, with string ExplainJobStep.Explanation rendering it as a plain-English clause.

ExplainJobWait.description: The durable wait a Suspended Job is blocked on: a signal name, or a timer and its due instant.

FiringFailurePolicyCode.description:
What happens to a scheduled definition's schedules when a firing fails for good: its attempts are
spent, or an exception is not retryable.

Known values:
- unspecified: Firing failure policy not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- continue: Default. A firing that fails for good leaves the definition's schedules scheduled; the next occurrence fires.
- pause-scheduling: A firing that fails for good pauses every schedule of the definition with a pause message until an operator resumes them.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

GetAlertResponse.description:
The single-alert read model returned by ValueTask<GetAlertResponse?> IAlerts.GetAsync(AlertRef alertRef, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)). It carries the list row's fields today and
is a distinct type because a detail read can grow additively (delivery history, the alerting event's detail)
without the list row paying for it. Two delivery fields read differently than their names suggest:
`RetryCount` is the attempts spent in the current send series, not over the row's life (a delivered send
ends the series and resets it), and `RetryAfterUtc` is the earliest instant the alert may be sent again, the
next retry while delivery is unsettled or the next reminder once it has settled, null when nothing is scheduled.

GetCalendarResponse.description:
One catalog calendar family as ValueTask<GetCalendarResponse?> ICalendars.GetAsync(CalendarLookup calendar, int? version = null, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) reads it: its role, `CurrentVersion` the Published
version (null while the family has none), `LatestVersion` the newest, and `ShownVersion` with its status and
its `Definition` JSON. ValueTask<ListCalendarVersionsResponse> ICalendars.ListVersionsAsync(ListCalendarVersionsQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) pages the versions and
ValueTask<ListCalendarDependentsResponse> ICalendars.ListDependentsAsync(ListCalendarDependentsQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) the schedules naming the family.

inputFormatName.description: The name of JobPayloadFormat GetDefinitionInputTemplateResponse.InputFormat, such as `json`, which is how the wire names a format.

GetDefinitionInputTemplateResponse.description:
The input contract of a registered job as operator tooling sees it: the job it was asked for, the CLR input type
name, the wire format its input serializes to, and (Json inputs only) a compile-time JSON skeleton the enqueue form
can seed its editor with. Compile-time facts from the generated manifest; the template is a shape hint, never a
contract and never a default value.

GetDefinitionResponse.description:
The whole `definitions` row ValueTask<GetDefinitionResponse?> IDefinitions.GetAsync(string jobNamespace, string jobName, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) returns, in column order: identity and
control, contract and formats, each policy as its code default, operator override (null inherits), and
effective value, and audit bookkeeping. The dashboard's definition editor reads it; the grid reads the slimmer
ListDefinitionsItem. A definition is addressed by namespace and name, and its catalog id stays off
the wire.

GetJobLineageMapChild.description: A direct child of the focused Job, linkable to its own detail view.

GetJobLineageMapNode.description:
A Job node in the lineage map - the focused Job or one of its ancestors. Carries the public
JobRef GetJobLineageMapNode.JobRef forms alongside the JSON-hidden numeric ids, matching ListJobsItem.

GetJobLineageMapResponse.description:
A compact runtime truth map for one focused Job, returned by ValueTask<GetJobLineageMapResponse?> IJobs.GetLineageMapAsync(JobLookup job, GetJobLineageMapOptions? options = null, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) for the
dashboard's lineage panel. `Ancestors` are context only (farthest first, immediate parent last, no steps of
their own), the nearest int GetJobLineageMapHandler.AncestorLimit; `Job` is the focused Job with its newest
int GetJobLineageMapHandler.StepLimit steps and the durable wait it is blocked on; `Children` are its
direct children up to int GetJobLineageMapOptions.ChildLimit. Each `HasMore` flags a truncated set.

GetJobLineageMapStep.description: One step of the focused Job, with string GetJobLineageMapStep.Explanation its status in plain English.

GetJobLineageMapWait.description: The durable wait the focused Job is blocked on: a signal, child latch, or timer, and its due instant.

GetJobResponse.description:
Read projection of a Job row exposed by `IJobs.GetAsync`: identity, linkage, status, scheduling, leasing,
retention, and input format; the input payload itself is never returned. Property order mirrors the `jobs`
entity (identity, scope and routing, caller keys, input) and then its 1:1 `jobs_state` row, so the shape reads
in schema order; a column resolved to a public value follows the id it came from, and the created/modified pair
closes the record. JSON carries the public refs and hides the numeric ids. `DefinitionId` is the surrogate
for the namespace+name pair, non-null because the row's definition_id is NOT NULL.

GetNamespaceResponse.description:
The single-namespace read model returned by ValueTask<GetNamespaceResponse?> INamespaces.GetAsync(string namespaceName, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)). It carries the same fields as
ListNamespacesItem today and is a distinct type because a detail read can grow additively without the
list row paying for it. `NamespaceId` is the DB-assigned id `jobs.namespace_id` references, internal and
never serialized, since a namespace is addressed by its unique kebab-case name; `Status` Active resolves at
enqueue and Suspended rejects it; `Version` is the row version a CAS control verb takes as expected.

GetOverviewResponse.description:
One-shot health counters for the dashboard overview, computed on the database clock: ready jobs (all Ready plus
Suspended jobs whose durable wait has expired) and the oldest one's claimable age, executing and failed jobs,
unresolved alerts and the Critical ones among them, dead workers and stale ones (Active or Draining, not seen
within the stale threshold), schedules due inside the due-soon window and the most overdue one's lag, and the
executor capacity across live workers, which `ExecutingCount` can exceed: a finished job stays Executing
until its batched completion write commits.

GetTenantResponse.description:
The single-tenant read model returned by ValueTask<GetTenantResponse?> ITenants.GetAsync(string tenantName, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)). It carries the same fields as
ListTenantsItem today and is a distinct type because a detail read can grow additively (usage counts,
per-tenant policy) without the list row paying for it. `TenantId` is the DB-assigned id
`jobs.tenant_id` references, internal and never serialized, since a tenant is addressed by its unique
`TenantName`; `Status` Active resolves at enqueue and Suspended rejects it; `Version` is the row
version a CAS control verb takes as expected.

GetWorkerResponse.description: Durable operator detail for one worker process registration.

JobKindCode.description:
What a `jobs` row is: an ordinary job, or the one permanent slot a scheduled definition fires through. The
kind is written at insert and never changes; the executor and the operator verbs read it instead of guessing from
a deduplication key or from the schedules a row happens to own.

Known values:
- unspecified: Job kind not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- ordinary: A job enqueued by an application, an operator, or a parent handler, or admitted by a schedule as a per-occurrence root; it ends in a terminal status.
- permanent-slot: The one reusable job of a scheduled definition; registration creates it, every firing of the definition's schedules runs through it, and it is never terminal by itself.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

JobPriorityCode.description:
Claim-priority value for `jobs_state.job_priority_code`. Discrete five-tier code-system enum
(`Bulk` / `Normal` / `High` / `Critical` / `Realtime`); no intermediate
values. Strict priority ordering on claim (no aging, no anti-starvation budget), so operators
isolate bulk workloads in their own `JobNamespace`. Set by the definition policy, definition
override, or per-enqueue priority override.

Known values:
- bulk: Lowest practical priority; bulk-class workloads.
- normal: Default priority. Most jobs use this.
- high: Above normal; operator opt-in for time-sensitive work.
- critical: Critical priority; close-to-realtime operator workloads.
- realtime: Highest priority.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

JobRef.description:
Public stable reference for one Job row: "job_" plus the Guid's 32 lowercase hex digits, such as
`job_01a14f4e954e7bf68ac609f3fcad8e3d`. Dashboards, HTTP APIs, and clients address jobs by this
value; the numeric JobId stays the internal engine identity. It copies and searches as one word,
and a UUIDv7 reads in creation order.

JobStatusCode.description:
Known values:
- unspecified: Job status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- ready: Eligible for claim; the claim path selects rows in this Status.
- blocked: Waiting behind an earlier unfinished job of its lane; the claim never offers it, and the settle of the job ahead promotes it to Ready.
- suspended: Parked and not progressing: awaiting an external signal via ctx.WaitSignalAsync, or awaiting children via ctx.WaitChildAsync / WaitChildrenAsync.
- paused: Not running, awaiting an external trigger to resume.
- idle: A permanent slot between firings: no outstanding firing, no lease, no claim time. Admission makes it Ready; it is never terminal.
- executing: Claimed by a worker under a live lease; its handler is running or about to start.
- succeeded: Terminal success.
- failed: Terminal failure: MaxAttempts exhausted, a non-retryable exception, an interrupted at-most-once step, or ctx.FailAsync.
- cancelled: Terminal cancellation by IJobs.CancelAsync or ctx.Cancel.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

One alert row in a ValueTask<ListAlertsResponse> IAlerts.ListAsync(ListAlertsQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) page. Channel configuration, endpoints, and deduplication keys
are delivery internals, never exposed by list reads. JSON carries the public job ref and hides the numeric job id;
the ref goes null once the subject job row is purged, since alerts outlive their job. `RetryCount` is the
attempts spent in the current send series (a delivered send ends it), and `RetryAfterUtc` the earliest instant
the alert may be sent again, the next retry while delivery is unsettled or the next reminder once settled.

ListSchedulesItem.description:
One schedule row in a ValueTask<ListSchedulesResponse> ISchedules.ListAsync(ListSchedulesQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) page. `NextOccurrenceAtUtc` is the next undecided occurrence;
`NextEvaluationAtUtc` and `EvaluationStatus` say when and why the engine next looks; `Status` is Active, Paused,
or Orphaned, with `PausedUntilUtc` for a timed pause; `Version` is the row version a CAS control verb takes as
expected; `JobRef` is the permanent slot's public ref, null for a PerOccurrence definition; `OutstandingCount` counts
its unsettled roots; the expiry pair is null together when unused, and `AvailabilityCalendarName` when the schedule
observes no availability calendar. The ids stay off the wire: the list pages by `ScheduleId` in its cursor.

One tenant row in a ValueTask<ListTenantsResponse> ITenants.ListAsync(ListTenantsQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) page, projected from the `tenants` table.
`TenantName` is the kebab-case name the caller registered, unique, and `DisplayName` the human label
(dashboards fall back to the name); `TenantId` is the DB-assigned id `jobs.tenant_id` references, internal
and never serialized, since a tenant is addressed by its key; `Status` Active resolves at enqueue and Suspended
rejects it; `Version` is the row version a CAS control verb takes as expected.

One worker row in a ValueTask<ListWorkersResponse> IWorkers.ListAsync(ListWorkersQuery query, CancellationToken ct = default(CancellationToken)) page: the registration's public ref and internal id, its
namespace and status, and what it reported at start (host machine, deployment version, engine version, runtime
framework, process id, executor cap), with the last heartbeat, start, and last change instants.

MisfireStrategyCode.description:
Known values:
- unspecified: Misfire strategy not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- catch-up-once: After downtime, fire once immediately for all missed occurrences, then resume from the next occurrence after now.
- skip: After downtime, skip all missed occurrences and resume from the first occurrence strictly after now.
- catch-up-latest: After downtime, fire once for the latest missed occurrence, the earlier ones coalesced into it, then resume from the next occurrence after now.
- catch-up-all: After downtime, fire every missed occurrence in order, one per settlement, subject to the schedule's capacity.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

NamespaceStatusCode.description:
Namespace state machine. 10-spaced ids; live states 10..80, mirroring
TenantStatusCode.

Known values:
- unspecified: Namespace status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- active: Namespace resolves at enqueue; enqueue allowed.
- suspended: Enqueue into the namespace is rejected and its schedules hold. Reversible (operator hold). Existing in-flight jobs are unaffected.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

OverdueDecisionCode.description:
Known values:
- unspecified: Overdue decision not recognized by this build; the value was written by a newer Acta.
- refuse: A publication with undecided overdue occurrences on a dependent schedule is rejected.
- discard: The old stream's undecided prefix is audited as skipped, and the new stream starts after now.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

PauseJobResponse.description: What pausing a job did, and the job's status and version after the attempt.

PauseScheduleResponse.description: What pausing a schedule did, and the schedule's state after the attempt.

PreviewCalendarItem.description: A schedule that names the family, as a publication would meet it: its path, binding, status, and overdue flag.

PreviewCalendarResponse.description:
A version's forecast beside the current version's over the same horizon, so an operator sees what a publication
adds and removes: instants for an occurrence calendar, windows for an availability calendar, and the bound
schedules with their overdue flag, which a Refuse publication would reject on: overdue ones first, at most
int PreviewCalendarHandler.ScheduleLimit, with `SchedulesTotal` and `OverdueTotal` counting them all.

PreviewScheduleResponse.description:
A read-only forecast of a schedule's upcoming fire instants, computed live (no persisted state is
read or written). string PreviewScheduleResponse.Expression and string PreviewScheduleResponse.TimeZoneId are the effective values
(operator override when present, else the original); IReadOnlyList<DateTime> PreviewScheduleResponse.NextOccurrencesUtc is strictly
increasing and may be shorter than requested when the expression is exhausted.

PublishCalendarResponse.description:
The outcome of a publication: Applied with the version now current and the schedules retimed (as
`job/schedule` paths), NotFound when the candidate is no version of the family, VersionConflict when the
current version is not the one the caller saw, or Rejected with the reason and, when the old version left overdue
occurrences undecided, the schedules holding them.

PurgeJobResponse.description: What purging a job did, and the job's status after the attempt; a purge carries no version.

RaiseJobSignalResponse.description: What raising a signal on a job did, and the job's status after the attempt; a raise carries no version.

RegisterTenantResponse.description:
The tenant a registration created or found: its stable numeric id, and its canonical key, which is how every other
call and route addresses it.

RemoveTagResponse.description: What removing one tag did: applied, or the target did not exist.

ReprioritizeJobResponse.description: What reprioritizing a job did, and the job's status and version after the attempt.

RequeueOutboxResponse.description: What parking a requeue of a source's quarantined rows did.

RescheduleJobResponse.description: What rescheduling a job did, and the job's status and version after the attempt.

ResolveAlertResponse.description: What resolving an alert did, and its timestamps after the attempt.

RestartJobResponse.description: What restarting a job did, and the job's status and version after the attempt.

ResumeJobResponse.description: What resuming a job did, and the job's status and version after the attempt.

ResumeNamespaceResponse.description: What resuming a namespace did, and the namespace's version after the attempt.

ResumeScheduleResponse.description: What resuming a schedule did, and the schedule's state after the attempt.

ResumeTenantResponse.description: What resuming a tenant did, and the tenant's version after the attempt.

RetireDefinitionResponse.description: What retiring a definition did, and the definition's version after the attempt.

definition.description: The calendar definition: a JSON object whose "kind" names its shape.

SaveCalendarDraftResponse.description:
What saving a draft did. Applied carries the new version and its content hash; Rejected carries each reason in
`Problems`, a compiler problem starting with its JSON path, and, when the store refused it, the family's latest
version, 0 for a family with none. A namespace no worker has run in yet is created, so the save never answers NotFound.

ScheduledDeliveryCode.description:
How a schedule delivers a definition's work: one permanent slot job fired again and again, or a fresh root job per
admitted occurrence. Immutable once the definition is registered.

Known values:
- unspecified: Scheduled delivery not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- permanent: Default. The definition's schedules fire one permanent slot job again and again.
- per-occurrence: Each admitted occurrence enqueues a fresh ordinary root job with its own state, retries, and retention.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

ScheduleExpireActionCode.description:
Known values:
- unspecified: Schedule expire action not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- discard: An occurrence older than the schedule's expiry when it is evaluated is skipped, audited with the reason expired, and the schedule moves on.
- pause: An occurrence older than the schedule's expiry when it is evaluated is skipped, audited with the reason expired, and the schedule is paused with the reason until an operator resumes it.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

ScheduleExpressionKindCode.description:
Known values:
- unspecified: Schedule expression kind not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- cron: Cron expression (Cronos dialect). Set at compile time by the source generator.
- interval: Interval duration: human (e.g. "5m") or ISO 8601 (e.g. "PT5M", "P1D"). Set at compile time by the source generator.
- calendar: A calendar named by the expression: its occurrences come from the bound calendar implementation. Set at compile time by the source generator.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

ScheduleFullBehaviorCode.description:
What a due occurrence does when its schedule already has its maximum of unsettled occurrences.

Known values:
- unspecified: Schedule full behavior not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- wait: Default. An occurrence of a full schedule stays undecided until a settlement frees capacity.
- drop: An occurrence of a full schedule is skipped, audited, and the schedule moves on.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

ScheduleOriginCode.description:
Known values:
- unspecified: Schedule origin not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- operator: Operator-driven schedule add/remove. No code path produces rows with this origin today.
- definition: Declared in [Schedule] attribute; refreshed by catalog upsert.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

ScheduleStatusCode.description:
Known values:
- unspecified: Schedule status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- active: Schedule is eligible to fire.
- paused: Operator-paused; does not fire until resumed, or until PausedUntilUtc passes when set.
- orphaned: Origin declaration disappeared from the catalog; set by reconciliation. Cannot fire or be paused/resumed.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

StepStatusCode.description:
State machine for `steps` rows. INSERT-once on first invocation (`Pending`);
UPDATE-in-place across retries; terminal transition to `Succeeded` (with `Result` populated),
`Exhausted` (parent receives `StepExhaustedException`), or `Interrupted` (an
`AtMostOnce` step re-entered before completion; parent receives `StepInterruptedException`). One row per
`(JobId, StepName)`; the framework never INSERTs a second step row for the same name.

Known values:
- unspecified: Step status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- pending: Step in flight or retrying within MaxAttempts / RetryWindow.
- succeeded: Step completed successfully; Result populated (or ResultFormatId = 0 for void steps).
- exhausted: Step exhausted retry budget; parent handler receives StepExhaustedException.
- interrupted: At-most-once step was re-entered before completion; outcome is unknown (ran 0 or 1 times). Parent receives StepInterruptedException.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

SuspendNamespaceResponse.description: What suspending a namespace did, and the namespace's version after the attempt.

SuspendTenantResponse.description: What suspending a tenant did, and the tenant's version after the attempt.

TagInput.description:
Caller-supplied per-tag wire row attached to an enqueued Job. Names are unique within a
request; string? TagInput.Value is null for presence-only tags.

TenantStatusCode.description:
Tenant state machine. 10-spaced ids; live states 10..80.

Known values:
- unspecified: Tenant status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- active: Tenant name resolves at enqueue; enqueue allowed.
- suspended: Admission suspended: new enqueues naming the tenant name are rejected, while already admitted jobs keep running and may expand through inherited children. Applies to enqueue transactions beginning after the suspend commits. Reversible (billing/abuse hold, admin pause).

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

TriggerScheduleResponse.description: What firing a schedule now did, and the schedule's state after the attempt.

UpdateDefinitionOverridesResponse.description: What setting a definition's policy overrides did, and the definition's version after the attempt.

input.description: Any JSON value, kept as sent.

UpdateJobInputResponse.description: What amending a job's input did, and the job's status after the attempt; an amend carries no version.

UpdateNamespaceResponse.description: What updating a namespace did, and the namespace's version after the attempt.

UpdateTenantResponse.description: What updating a tenant did, and the tenant's version after the attempt.

UpsertTagResponse.description: What upserting one tag did: applied, or the target did not exist.

WorkerStatusCode.description:
Lifecycle status of a worker row. Mirrors the JobStatusCode band scheme: live states 10..90,
terminal success at 100, terminal error at 200+.

Known values:
- unspecified: Worker status not recognized by this build; the row was written by a newer Acta.
- active: Polling claim; accepting work.
- draining: Worker stopped polling; finishing in-flight.
- stopped: Worker shut down cleanly; terminal success.
- dead: Heartbeat went stale; crash recovery reclaims lapsed leases, and a resumed heartbeat makes it Active again.

Other values may appear: keep a value this client does not know as it is.

ActaControl.name: X-Acta-Control
ActaControl.description: Confirms a control call. The value is true; a missing header or any other value answers 400.
